description.value: A cross-sectional optimized voxel-based morphometry study examining grey matter volume associations with years of cocaine use and duration of abstinence in abstinent cocaine users, with comparison to drug-naïve controls.

spans.text: The aim of the present study, using a cross-sectional design, was to examine volume differences in cortical grey matter in a sample of former cocaine addicts who varied in length of abstinence and duration of use.

value: We hypothesized that abstinence duration would be associated with a set of GM volume changes in regions critical to executive function, specifically anterior cingulate and lateral prefrontal cortex.
We further hypothesized that any GM volume changes that may be attributable to length of use would be distinct from those related to abstinence duration.

description.value: Cross-sectional observational study of abstinent cocaine users and age-matched drug-naïve controls.

spans.text: The cross-sectional design employed here suffers by being unable to resolve whether effects related to abstinence duration arose from abstinence or preceded abstinence.
Participants were divided into two groups: one group of 43 abstinent cocaine users (2 female) and a second of 43 age-matched controls (7 female).

definition.value: Four regions showed positive correlations with years of use, that is grey matter volume increased in these regions with longer terms of use.

value: Grey matter volume increased in several regions with longer terms of use, including bilateral precentral gyrus, left medial frontal gyrus, and right cerebellar nodule.

definition.value: Several regions displayed negative correlations with years of use.

value: Several regions displayed negative correlations with years of use, indicating lower grey matter volume with longer terms of use; these included the right cerebellar tonsil, bilateral superior temporal and inferior frontal gyri, right anterior insula, right subcallosal gyrus, and right anterior cingulate gyrus.

definition.value: A number of regions were observed to show positive correlations with weeks of abstinence, that is grey matter volume in these regions increased with abstinence.

value: Grey matter volume increased with weeks of abstinence in the left insula, bilateral cingulate gyri, left cuneus, bilateral superior frontal gyri, left cerebellar culmen, and right middle temporal gyrus. In these regions, shorter-abstinent users had less grey matter than controls, whereas longer-abstinent users had greater volumes; the average crossover point was 35.6 weeks of abstinence.

definition.value: Three regions were observed to display negative correlations with length of abstinence.

value: Three regions displayed negative correlations with length of abstinence, including bilateral cuneus and the left precuneus. In these regions, grey matter reached control levels after an average of 24.2 weeks of abstinence and then declined further with increased abstinence duration.

spans.text: All scanning was conducted on a 1.5T Siemens VISION scanner (Erlangen, Germany) at NKI that was equipped with a 30.5-cm i.d. three-axis local gradient coil and an end-capped quadrature birdcage radio-frequency head coil.

High-resolution T1-weighted MPRAGE anatomical images were acquired with the following parameters: TE = 4.9 ms, TR = 11.6 ms, flip angle 8°, FOV 300 mm, 1.2 mm isotropic voxels, matrix 256×256, and 172 sagittal slices.

model_settings.value: The model included weeks of abstinence, years of use prior to abstinence, and age as a nuisance covariate.

spans.text: The two variables of interest, weeks of abstinence and years of use prior to abstinence were included in a single voxelwise whole-brain regression model. Since years of use could be a proxy for age and given the well-established relationship between age and GM volume  [28] ,  [40] , age was also included as a nuisance covariate in the regression model.
The voxelwise regression coefficients and associated T statistics for each regression term were then split into maps of positive and negative coefficients.

spans.text: The data were median filtered (3×3 voxels), brain-extracted using AFNI’s 3dSkullStrip  [30] , and then segmented into grey and white matter and cerebrospinal fluid  [31] .
The modulated segmented images were then smoothed with an isotropic Gaussian kernel (σ = 2 mm ∼ 4.7 mm FWHM).

STG: Superior Temporal Gyrus, IFG: Inferior Frontal Gyrus, AI: Anterior Insula. BA: Brodmann Area. Crossover point refers to the location on the x-axis (years of use or weeks of abstinence) where the regression (solid) line for the CD users intersects with the mean of the control participants (dashed line). Term refers to the term of interest in the regression model (years of use or weeks of abstinence) from which the clusters were derived. Polarity refers to the sign (positive or negative) of the regression coefficients from which the cluster was generated.
